newsitem.title: USA: Jackson denies he considering presidential run.
newsitem.headline: Jackson denies he considering presidential run.

text.p: Civil rights leader Jesse Jackson Saturday called a Time magazine story that said he was unhappy with the White House and that he may run again for president was "conjecture."

"To conclude that I'm unhappy with the White House and running for president is conjecture, it's a diversion and it's really not fair," Jackson said in a telephone interview following his weekly address at his Rainbow Push Action Network headquarters on Chicago's South Side.

"Their story is very misleading," Jackson said of the magazine article. "There is no basis for saying that I'm unhappy with the White House, and I have not spoken with anyone about running in the year 2000."
Time quoted an unnamed long-time friend and campaign adviser of Jackson's as saying: "I've never seen him so serious so soon about running."
Jackson ran for the Democratic presidential nomination in 1984 and 1988.

Jackson also brushed off the Time story's contention that he was courting an unlikely new soul-mate, Republican House Speaker Newt Gingrich or that he would be Gingrich's personal guest at Tuesday's State of the Union address by President Clinton.

Jackson said Gingrich, in contrast to two years ago when he ascended his post as speaker, has shown an openness to hearing about black American's concerns and has made a gesture by reaching out to members of the Congressional Black Caucus.

"Talking with Gingrich is simply (that) I realise we are going to deal with the matter of welfare reform and not be violent towards people in need, keep opening closed doors ... and develop some plan to reinvest in America," Jackson said.

Jackson said the Speaker's office is routinely in charge of giving out tickets to the State of the Union, and that if he is seated beside Gingrich's wife in the family's box in the Speaker's gallery, that was Gingrich's office's decision.
The article published Saturday in Time said Jackson and Gingrich have been "communing since Gingrich's opening day speech to the House (in January)."
